claims.claim: An external party solicited confidential data from the insider
claims.rationale: ART-002 emails from spy.conspirator@nist.gov explicitly request 'more data' and 'the remaining data'

claims.claim: Confidential corporate files were collected from a secured network drive and staged locally
claims.rationale: ART-005 shows connection to \\10.11.11.128\secured_drive, file copy to Desktop\$ data, then disconnect

claims.claim: File extensions were deliberately altered to conceal content
claims.rationale: ART-003 shows .docx->.mp3 and .pptx->.jpg renames of files classified confidential

claims.claim: Data was exfiltrated via personal Google Drive/Gmail
claims.rationale: ART-004 shows Google Drive login with personal Gmail, files uploaded and shared, 'Login is below.' email

claims.claim: Anti-forensic tools were installed to destroy evidence after exfiltration
claims.rationale: ART-004 notes CCleaner and Eraser installed after the upload
ART-001 logon/rename timestamps at the 16:00 policy boundary; consistent with concealment but secondary

null_hypothesis_considered: An employee legitimately accessing project files and using personal cloud storage for convenient backup, with CCleaner/Eraser run merely for routine disk cleanup.
verdict_rationale: Coordinated chain - external solicitation, selective collection of confidential files from a secured drive, extension masquerading, exfil to a personal cloud account, and post-act anti-forensic wiping - rules out the benign convenience explanation and confirms deliberate malicious insider exfiltration.
